newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco do Brasil, IBM sign software deal.
newsitem.headline: Banco do Brasil, IBM sign software deal.

text.p: Banco do Brasil, the largest bank in Latin America, signed an agreement Friday with IBM's local software unit to update and standardize its basic software platform, the firms said.

The accord, aimed at automating all Banco do Brasil branches and service points nationwide, calls for $13 million in investment in software, education and technological support through 2000, the companies said in a statement.
Under the deal, the bank and IBM Brazil Software Division will also form a technological partnership creating a Software Technologies Development Center in Brasilia, the statement said.
The agreement calls for IBM's Brazil unit to install IBM software products in 6,000 local networks, with 4,800 nodes in Banco do Brasil branches and service points.
The accord was signed in Brasilia by bank President Paulo Ximenes and IBM president for software worldwide Stanley J. Krasnow, officials said.
